title: Flourishing From Within: Reclaiming the Human Potential at the Heart of Positive Psychology
abstract: Since its emergence, positive psychology has sought to identify the conditions that support human flourishing. Despite substantial empirical advances, the field continues to face conceptual fragmentation and lacks a widely accepted unifying philosophical foundation. This article offers a humanistic re-visioning of flourishing grounded in three organizing metaphors—Universal Mind, Consciousness, and Thought—reframed in contemporary psychological language. Rather than locating wellbeing primarily in the cultivation of strengths or favorable conditions, the proposed “inside-out” perspective suggests that flourishing reflects an intrinsic human capacity that may become obscured through habitual patterns of thought. From this perspective, growth is understood less as the acquisition of positive traits than as the rediscovery of psychological openness evident in moments of insight, presence, and authentic encounter. Intended as a conceptual and phenomenologically informed contribution, the framework employs these metaphors heuristically rather than metaphysically. By integrating philosophical reflection with implications for practice and social change, the article invites positive psychology to move toward a more principle-centered understanding of human potential grounded in meaning, agency, and human development.
